## What Is PDE Data?

**PDE = Prescription Drug Event** — the record of prescription-drug fills under Medicare Part D.

- Whenever a Part D beneficiary fills a prescription, the plan submits a PDE record summarizing the fill event
- PDE data are **standardized** — not raw transactional claims but CMS-defined summary extracts

---

## Why PDE Matters / Who Reports It

- All Part D plan sponsors (stand-alone PDPs and Medicare Advantage plans with drug benefits) must report PDE data to CMS for **every covered fill**
- Provides a **comprehensive view** of outpatient prescription drug utilization among Medicare beneficiaries under Part D

---

## PDE Data Contents — Core Variables

PDE records include many standardized fields. Key ones:

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| Beneficiary ID | Encrypted unique identifier |
| Prescription fill date | Date the drug was dispensed |
| Brand & generic drug names | Drug identification |
| Dosage form & strength | Formulation details |
| Quantity & days supply | Utilization metrics |
| Coverage & payment | Cost and subsidy data |

## What PDE Captures — And What It Doesn't

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**✅ What it captures:**

- Detailed outpatient prescription drug fills under Part D
- Timing, drug identity, strength, quantity, payment data
- Enables utilization, adherence, cost, and drug-exposure analyses
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**⚠️ Limitations:**

- Drugs administered during hospitalizations may not appear
- Dispensed ≠ ingested (no guarantee drug was taken)
- Limited clinical context — must link with other Medicare files
- Doesn't capture drugs not covered by Part D (OTC, hospital-administered)
:::

:::

---

## How Researchers Use PDE Data

1. **Define medication exposure periods** — when a drug was filled, days supply
2. **Study drug utilization patterns** — adherence (MPR, gaps), polypharmacy
3. **Link with Medicare claims** — inpatient, outpatient, diagnoses for health outcomes, safety, pharmacoepidemiology
4. **Cost and utilization analyses** — what drugs, how often, cost burden, subsidies

---

## Why Request the Part D Drug Characteristics File

| | PDE File Only | PDE + Drug Characteristics File |
|---|---|---|
| Drug ID | NDC code only | Brand + generic name |
| Strength | ❌ None | ✅ Exact (e.g., 10 mg, 20 mg) |
| Dosage form | ❌ None | ✅ Tablet, capsule, solution |
| Brand vs. generic | ❌ Cannot distinguish | ✅ Enables comparison |
| Drug exposure | Limited clinical definition | ✅ Clinically meaningful |
| Dose analyses | ❌ Not sufficient | ✅ Dose-response supported |

---

## National Drug Codes (NDC) Explained

**Example:** NDC for a 100-count bottle of Prozac 20 mg → `0777-3105-02`

| Segment | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Labeler code** | `0777` | Dista Products Co. (manufacturer of Prozac) |
| **Product code** | `3105` | Identifies strength, dosage form (capsule) |
| **Package code** | `02` | Package size (100 capsules per bottle) |

---

## Brand Name vs. Generic Name in PDE

- **Generic name** = scientific/chemical name (used in datasets, PDE, research)
- **Brand name** = marketing name from the drug company
- One generic can have **multiple brand names**

| Generic Name | Brand Name | Main Use |
|---|---|---|
| Atorvastatin | Lipitor | Cholesterol |
| Metformin | Glucophage | Type 2 Diabetes |
| Lisinopril | Prinivil / Zestril | Blood pressure |
| Amlodipine | Norvasc | Blood pressure |
| Omeprazole | Prilosec | Acid reflux |
